animals.description: The Bornean Orangutan is a super-smart "person of the forest" that shares almost the same DNA as us! They are the biggest animals in the world that live mostly in trees, where they build cozy new nests out of branches every single night. Grown-up males have big, wide faces and a special throat pouch to make "long calls" that echo through the jungle. These clever apes are great at using tools—they even make umbrellas out of leaves to stay dry! By eating fruit and spreading seeds, they act like forest gardeners, helping new trees grow across the island of Borneo.

threats.explanation: Bornean Orangutans are hunted for bushmeat and killed when they venture into agricultural areas in search of food.

questions.questionText: What is the scientific name of the Malayan Tiger?
questions.explanation: The Malayan Tiger's subspecies name jacksoni honours tiger conservationist Peter Jackson. Together with Panthera tigris it forms the full scientific name.

questions.questionText: Where do Malayan Tigers mainly live?
questions.explanation: Malayan Tigers inhabit the dense tropical rainforests of Peninsular Malaysia, where thick vegetation and prey are abundant.

questions.questionText: What do Malayan Tigers usually eat?
questions.explanation: As apex carnivores, Malayan Tigers hunt large prey including sambar deer, barking deer, and wild boar in the forest.

choices.choiceText: Deer, wild boar, and other animals

questions.questionText: How many Malayan Tigers are estimated to be left in the wild?
questions.explanation: Fewer than 150 individuals are believed to remain in the wild, making this one of the most critically endangered big cats on Earth.

questions.questionText: Why are Malayan Tigers endangered?
questions.explanation: Rapid deforestation for agriculture and illegal poaching for body parts have drastically reduced the Malayan Tiger population over decades.

questions.questionText: What colour are Malayan Tigers?
questions.explanation: Like most tigers, Malayan Tigers have a distinctive orange coat with dark black stripes that provide camouflage in the forest.

questions.questionText: The Malayan Tiger is the national symbol of which country?
questions.explanation: The Malayan Tiger (Harimau Malaya) is Malaysia's national animal and appears on the national coat of arms supporting the shield.

questions.questionText: What is the role of the Malayan Tiger in the ecosystem?
questions.explanation: As a top predator, the Malayan Tiger regulates prey populations, which in turn keeps the forest ecosystem balanced and healthy.

questions.questionText: What is the scientific name of the Malaysia Sun Bear?
questions.explanation: Helarctos means "sun bear" in Greek, and malayanus refers to the Malay Peninsula — together naming this Southeast Asian species.

questions.questionText: Where do Sun Bears mainly live?
questions.explanation: Sun Bears are found across the tropical rainforests of Southeast Asia, including Malaysia, Indonesia, and Thailand, where they forage in trees.

questions.questionText: What is the Sun Bear's favourite food?
questions.explanation: Sun Bears are famous for raiding beehives using their long tongues. They also eat termites, beetles, and other insects they dig out of logs.

questions.questionText: What type of diet does the Sun Bear have?
questions.explanation: Sun Bears eat a wide variety of foods including fruits, honey, insects, small vertebrates, and plant matter, making them true omnivores.

questions.questionText: What special marking does the Sun Bear have on its chest?
questions.explanation: The Sun Bear has a distinctive pale yellow or orange U-shaped patch on its chest, resembling a rising sun, which gives it its name.

questions.questionText: Why are Sun Bears important for the rainforest?
questions.explanation: By eating fruits and excreting seeds elsewhere, Sun Bears aid seed dispersal. They also control insect populations by eating termites and beetles.

choices.choiceText: They help spread seeds and control insects
They make honey for other animals

questions.questionText: What is the Sun Bear's conservation status on the IUCN Red List?
questions.explanation: The IUCN lists Sun Bears as Vulnerable due to habitat loss from deforestation and hunting for the exotic pet and bile trade.

questions.questionText: The Sun Bear is the _______ bear species in the world.
questions.explanation: Sun Bears are the smallest of the eight bear species, with adults typically weighing only 25–65 kg compared to a grizzly's 200+ kg.

questions.questionText: What is the scientific name of the Borneo Orang Utan?
questions.explanation: Pongo is the genus for orang utans, and pygmaeus (meaning "dwarf") distinguishes the Bornean species from the Sumatran Pongo abelii.

questions.questionText: What does the name "Orang Utan" mean in the Malay language?
questions.explanation: "Orang" means person and "utan" (hutan) means forest in Malay — a fitting name for these highly intelligent great apes.

questions.questionText: In Malaysia, where are Orang Utans mainly found?
questions.explanation: Bornean Orang Utans live in the rainforests of Sabah and Sarawak, the Malaysian states on the island of Borneo.

questions.questionText: What is the favourite food of Orang Utans?
questions.explanation: Orang Utans love wild figs as a dietary staple. They also eat durian — the pungent fruit beloved in Malaysia — along with other forest fruits.

questions.questionText: How do Orang Utans help the rainforest grow?
questions.explanation: Orang Utans eat large fruits and travel widely, depositing seeds far from the parent tree through their droppings, helping forests regenerate.

choices.choiceText: They spread seeds through the forest

questions.questionText: What is the conservation status of the Borneo Orang Utan on the IUCN Red List?
questions.explanation: Critically Endangered is the highest threat level before Extinct in the Wild. Rapid deforestation and habitat fragmentation are the primary causes.

questions.questionText: Where do Orang Utans spend most of their lives?
questions.explanation: Orang Utans are almost entirely arboreal, spending their lives in the forest canopy where they build nests from branches and leaves each night.

questions.questionText: What is the biggest threat to Orang Utans in Malaysia?
questions.explanation: Large-scale clearing of rainforest for palm oil plantations, logging, and agriculture has destroyed much of the Orang Utan's natural habitat.

funFacts.factText: The Sun Bear is the SMALLEST bear species in the entire world — much smaller than a polar bear!
The Malayan Tiger is found ONLY in Peninsular Malaysia — nowhere else in the world!
"Orang Utan" means "Person of the Forest" in the Malay language — a truly amazing name!
The pale U-shaped patch on its chest looks like a rising sun — that is exactly how it got its name!
The Malayan Tiger is the national symbol of Malaysia and appears on the national coat of arms!
Orang Utans share 96.9% of their DNA with humans — making them one of our closest animal relatives!
The Sun Bear has a tongue up to 25 cm long — it uses it to lick honey and insects out of tree holes!
Malayan Tigers are nocturnal hunters — they are most active and hunt mostly at night!
Orang Utans have arms longer than their entire body — perfect for swinging gracefully between trees!
Sun Bears are excellent tree climbers and love to sleep and sunbathe high up in the trees!
Malayan Tigers can grow up to 2.5 metres long — that is as long as a small car!
Orang Utans are very clever — they tear off large leaves and hold them over their heads as umbrellas in the rain!
Sun Bears are sometimes called "Honey Bears" because honey is one of their absolute favourite foods!
Fewer than 150 Malayan Tigers are estimated to be left in the wild today — they are Critically Endangered!
Baby Orang Utans stay with their mothers for up to 12 years — the longest childhood of any wild animal!
Every tiger has a completely unique stripe pattern — just like human fingerprints, no two are the same!
Orang Utans are the "gardeners of the forest" — they spread seeds everywhere they travel, helping new trees grow!
Sun Bears have very strong curved claws that help them tear open tree trunks to find insects and honey!
